title: The sedimentary kaolinitic clays of South Carolina [chapter 2]
citation: Lang, W.B., 1940, The sedimentary kaolinitic clays of South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Bulletin 901, map scale 1:62,500.
notes:
USGS Bulletin 901 (1940), Clay investigations in the southern States; the cataloged part is chapter 2, The sedimentary kaolinitic clays of South Carolina (Lang). Packet 1 (plate 2 and pages 2-43): front matter, chapter 1 introduction (multi-state; only the South Carolina summary applies), and the start of chapter 2 (history, rubber and paper clay properties, rubber-test tables, colored clays, overburden ratio, reserves). Rubber-compound test results (tensile strength, elongation, hardness) and the Chicora pit iron analysis are clay-product tests that do not fit the schema; plate 2 (geologic map of the Aiken area) and plate 1 map faces are OCR noise and not itemized. Texas, Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia and Florida content left out. SUBSURFACE: none in this packet.
Packet 2 (pp. 44-84): chapter 2 continued - Tuscaloosa, McBean and Barnwell formations, Huber test well (Langley), driller's log of a nearby water well, buhrstone, warping, prospecting methods, record of prospecting tests 1-56 (pp. 63-74), and ceramic test samples 1-12. The record of tests 5-56 (pp. 64-74) is badly garbled in the text layer: most descriptions, several test numbers and locations are missing; only rows whose description, thickness and depth sit on one line are recorded (tops computed from depth minus thickness, flagged inferred); tests 5, 6, 17, 24, 26, 27, 29, 31, 33, 43, 45, 51, 53, 55 left out or location only. A page-image re-read of pp. 64-74 is queued. Driller's log (p. 53): row '105 65' is an OCR misread (probably 165/65) and is left out; row descriptions missing. Ceramic test results (water of plasticity, shrinkage, modulus of rupture, absorption, residue) are clay-product tests that do not fit the schema and are left out. Figures 3-7 (sections and sketch maps) are labels only. SUBSURFACE: Huber test well sample descriptions (samples 1-50, pp. 47-52) not itemized beyond the generalized section; heavy-mineral lists left in descriptions only; tests 5-56 total depths not recorded where the last row cannot be tied to a test.
Packet 3 (pp. 85-118): end of chapter 2 (ceramic samples 12-31 with pit sections, summary, supplemental note on waters of the Horse Creek area with partial water analyses) and chapter 3, The bleaching clays of South Carolina (Bay), pp. 96-105. Pages 106-118 are chapter 4 (San Antonio area and Morris County, Texas) and are not read for values. Ceramic test results and bleach ratings (raw and acid-treated G/Y/R/B) are clay-product tests that do not fit the schema and are left out; the bleaching-clay localities are recorded as observations with the formation from the table section heading. Page 103 (a rotated part of the Barnwell bleaching-clay table) is unreadable in the text layer and is skipped; the Clarendon (Paxville) and Williamsburg (Kingstree) Black Mingo rows are too garbled to record. Water analyses (p. 93): bicarbonate row has five values for six columns and the date row five dates for six columns, so neither can be assigned and both are left out (only the Horse Creek date, April 3, 1935, is given in the text); iron for analysis 6 is printed "' 260.28" (garbled) and left out. pH has no printed units. Immaculate Kaolin Co. test hole 56 (p. 88) may or may not be prospecting test 56 of p. 74; recorded separately. SUBSURFACE: Chicora pit clay sections are given as depths below top of the clay bed (not land surface) and are kept as descriptions.
Packet 4 (pp. 119-158): chapter 4, clay deposits of the San Antonio area and Morris County, Texas. No South Carolina content; nothing recorded.
Packet 5 (pp. 159-193): chapter 4 continued (San Antonio area and Morris County, Texas). No South Carolina content; nothing recorded.
